claim: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners allow passwordless sudo and their kernel ships sch_cake/sch_netem/sch_htb modules so the full experiment suite (including the CAKE reference) can run in CI.
evidence: (1) Passwordless sudo: GitHub's official runner reference states verbatim "The Linux and macOS virtual machines both run using passwordless sudo." ubuntu-latest is listed alongside ubuntu-24.04 and both link to the Ubuntu 24.04 image readme. (2) Kernel modules: the current actions/runner-images Ubuntu2404 readme (image 20261012.334.1) reports OS 24.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure, iproute2 6.1.0-1ubuntu6.4 installed. The Ubuntu package file list for linux-modules-6.17.0-1022-azure (noble-updates, amd64) contains /lib/modules/6.17.0-1022-azure/kernel/net/sched/sch_cake.ko.zst, sch_netem.ko.zst, sch_htb.ko.zst and sch_fq_codel.ko.zst, i.e. all four qdiscs are in the base linux-modules package (not linux-modules-extra, which is the package historically missing/unmatchable on Azure runners per community discussion 63910). Contents searches for sch_cake.ko, sch_netem.ko and sch_htb.ko across noble-updates likewise show them only in linux-modules-* packages, never linux-modules-extra-*. (3) Weakness of the offered support URL: the packages.ubuntu.com query for suite=noble only lists the original release kernels (e.g. linux-modules-6.8.0-1007-azure), not the 6.17 HWE azure kernel actually running on ubuntu-latest, so it is indirect; the noble-updates file list is the relevant primary source. (4) Not verified: I could not find a public workflow log or repo that demonstrably runs `tc qdisc ... cake` or modprobe of these modules on ubuntu-latest (grep.app rate-limited; web searches returned nothing CI-specific), and no workflow in this project has been executed. Module presence in the installed package set strongly implies `sudo modprobe`/auto-load via tc will work, but it is an inference, not an observed run.
correction: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest (Ubuntu 24.04, image 20261012.334.1, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure) runs with passwordless sudo per GitHub's official docs, and the installed base package linux-modules-6.17.0-1022-azure ships sch_cake, sch_netem, sch_htb and sch_fq_codel as loadable modules, so the qdiscs needed for the experiment suite and the CAKE reference should be available via `sudo tc`/`sudo modprobe`. However: (a) the cited packages.ubuntu.com link shows the noble release kernel (6.8.0-1007-azure), not the kernel the runners actually boot, so the proper evidence is the noble-updates file list for the running kernel; (b) the kernel version rotates with each image release, so the workflow should check `uname -r` and `sudo modprobe sch_cake sch_netem sch_htb` as a first step rather than assume; (c) no execution has been observed, and shaping must be applied to lo/veth/netns rather than the runner's primary interface to avoid breaking the job; shared-VM timing jitter also limits how precise latency measurements in CI can be.
impact_on_candidate: Low risk. The CI-reproducibility differentiator and CAKE comparison are well supported by primary sources, so the case study can keep them. Remaining exposure is operational rather than factual: the team should (1) add a smoke step in the workflow that loads the three modules and fails fast with a clear message if the image's kernel changes, (2) run experiments inside a network namespace / veth pair, and (3) present CI results as reproducibility/regression checks rather than precision latency benchmarks, since GitHub runners are shared VMs. If the modules were ever dropped from a future azure kernel, the fallback would be a self-hosted runner or a nested VM/container with a generic kernel, which would weaken but not eliminate the differentiator.
